items.q: How do I choose between a PDA and a tablet?
items.a: Start with the task. A PDA is better for one-handed scanning in aisles, on a ladder or in the field. A tablet is better when the operator needs a larger screen, Windows software, equipment ports or a vehicle mount. The workflow review on our Solutions page describes the usual patterns.

items.q: Are the specifications on this site final?
items.a: Only confirmed values are shown. Configuration-dependent items are confirmed against the approved datasheet for your SKU, because modules, memory, OS versions and regional approvals vary between models and markets.

items.q: Can you configure modules for a specific project?
items.a: Yes, subject to the selected platform. Barcode engines, RFID modules, NFC, document readers, memory and accessories are reviewed against the application, target market and production plan. Some options require tooling or minimum quantities.

items.q: How do I compare two models for my workflow?
items.a: Send us the workflow, environment, target market and expected volume. We will narrow the range and confirm the configuration, accessories and documentation path for each option.

items.q: What information should I include in an inquiry?
items.a: The workflow or task, the target market, the expected quantity and any required capture method (barcode, UHF RFID, mobile print or document reading). If you already have a device or software platform in mind, include it.

items.q: Will I receive a datasheet before ordering?
items.a: Yes. Once the model and target market are clear, we provide the applicable datasheet and confirm the configuration-dependent values. For some models the public page shows only confirmed values, with the full sheet available on request.

items.q: Do you support samples?
items.a: Sample and pilot policy is agreed per project. For configured products, a prototype or pilot build is the usual acceptance step before a production order.

items.q: Can you sign an NDA?
items.a: Yes, where the project involves confidential workflow, software or commercial information. Raise it in the inquiry and we will agree the process before detailed information is exchanged.

items.q: Do you handle OEM / ODM inquiries through the same form?
items.a: Yes. Select the cooperation interest in the form and describe the branding, configuration or development requirement. The OEM / ODM page describes the three engagement models and the six-stage process.

items.q: How are regional approvals handled?
items.a: Certification scope depends on the target market, device configuration and applicable standard. We review the requirement during discovery and confirm the documentation path for the selected configuration.

process.body: Each stage has a defined output and an acceptance point. We do not move to the next gate until both sides agree the previous one is closed.

steps.title: Discovery

faq.body: If your question is not covered here, include it in the project inquiry. We will answer it against the specific platform and market.

items.q: Can we put our logo on the device and packaging?
items.a: Yes, within the scope agreed for the project. Logo application, boot animation, labels, packaging and manuals are reviewed together because they affect tooling, minimum quantities and artwork approval.

items.q: What is the minimum order quantity?
items.a: It depends on the platform, configuration and branding scope. Private-label projects usually have a different threshold from full project development. The MOQ is defined in the proposal after the requirement review.

items.q: Can you preload our application and MDM profile?
items.a: Software image and preload can be discussed as part of the configured-product model. The exact scope — preload list, MDM enrollment, regional settings and update responsibility — is documented before prototyping.

items.q: Do you support regional RFID bands and approvals?
items.a: UHF RFID frequency bands and market approvals differ by country. We confirm the target market before selecting the module and include the applicable configuration in the proposal.

items.q: Can we receive samples before a production order?
items.a: Sample policy and lead time are agreed per project. For configured products, a prototype or pilot build is the usual acceptance step before mass production.

items.q: Who owns tooling and documentation?
items.a: Ownership, change notification and documentation rights are defined in the project agreement. We recommend agreeing these before tooling or artwork is released.

items.q: What certifications can you support?
items.a: Certification scope depends on the target market, the device configuration and the applicable standard. We review the requirement during discovery and align the document package accordingly.

cta.body: Tell us the application, target market, expected volume and branding scope. We will come back with the right platform and a project path.
